definition: A model that processes and connects more than one modality, most commonly text and images.
details: Multimodal models learn a shared representation space so that concepts can be transferred across senses — for example, matching an image to a caption that describes it. CLIP trained image and text encoders on 400 million image–text pairs using contrastive learning, enabling zero-shot image classification and powering later generation pipelines.

explainer.lead: A multimodal model processes and connects more than one modality, most commonly text and images. It matters because a shared representation lets concepts transfer across senses.

tiers.eli5: Like a person who can match a photo to the sentence that describes it because both mean the same thing to them.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train encoders on paired data so matching concepts land near each other in a shared space, enabling zero-shot classification and generation pipelines. A pitfall is that alignment quality depends on the scale and coverage of the paired data.
tiers.paperLevel: Models learn a shared representation space so concepts transfer across modalities; CLIP trained image and text encoders on 400 million image–text pairs with contrastive learning. Limits: transfer depends on the breadth of the training pairs.

explainer.example: CLIP scores an image against candidate text labels and picks the best match, classifying images into categories it was never explicitly trained on.

citation.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
